Zareby Koscielne New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zaręby Kościelne, Poland

Not demolished. One of two historic Jewish cemeteries in Zaręby, this newer site was likely founded in the first half of the 19th century, east of the market square toward Grabów, covering about 1.7 hectares (see town notes below for the older cemetery's separate, undocumented fate). Zaręby, first mentioned in 1410 and granted German location rights in 1448, recorded its first Jews in 1638; a 1680 Jewish school preceded designated cemetery land, and the settlement gained town rights in 1732. Population reached 31.7% (1,959) by the late 19th century, rising to 88% by 1939. This newer cemetery was likely destroyed during WWII and formally closed for burials in 1961; on September 28, 1941, most of Zaręby's Jews (about 2,000 people) were shot by Germans in an anti-tank pit near Mianówek while being marched to the Czyżewo ghetto - a monument now marks that massacre site.
